# hostc

> hostc gives a local HTTP or WebSocket server a public HTTPS URL. No account, nothing to install beyond Node.js 22+.

## Start a tunnel

Run it as a long-lived background process, pointing at the local server's port:

    npx hostc@latest 3000

Other targets: `127.0.0.1:8080` (host and port) or a full origin such as `https://localhost:5173`. Always use `npx hostc@latest`; never install it globally (`npm i -g`) or add it to package.json, which pins a version that stops working when the server updates. An outdated CLI exits with a message telling you to upgrade.

The public URL is the first `https://` URL printed, on its own line:

      https://k7m2xq9pa4dn.hostc.app  → http://localhost:3000

Read it from the output; never guess it. Afterwards hostc logs one line per request: time, method, status, path, duration.

## While it runs

- The URL works only while hostc runs. Do not wait for the process to exit.
- On a network drop or server restart hostc reconnects by itself and keeps the URL, for up to 10 minutes offline. After that it prints "The tunnel expired while offline. It has a new URL:" followed by the new URL; give the user the new one.
- Local dev servers that check Host or Origin (Vite, Next.js) work without configuration. WebSockets, hot reload and Server-Sent Events work.
- If hostc warns "Nothing is listening on …", start the local server first; hostc keeps running and forwards once it is up.

## Stop it

Send SIGINT (Ctrl+C) or SIGTERM. The URL stops working immediately. Starting hostc again always gives a new URL.

Exit codes: 0 stopped or help/version, 1 could not create or keep the tunnel (read the printed error), 2 invalid arguments.

## Errors a visitor can get

- 404 Tunnel not found: wrong URL, or the tunnel was stopped or expired.
- 502 Tunnel offline: hostc is reconnecting or was killed.
- 502 Local server unavailable: the local server is not running on that port or crashed.
- 504 Local server timed out: no response started within 120 seconds.
- 503 Tunnel busy: 256 requests and WebSockets already in flight.

## Safety

Anyone with the URL reaches the local server. Only expose what the user asked to share; never databases, admin panels or anything holding secrets. Stop the tunnel when it is no longer needed.

Source and self-hosting: https://github.com/akazwz/hostc
